nodes.title: shukka v1 works end to end on a test consumer
nodes.description:
Serves R1-R8 and R10 in docs/factory/v1/requirements.md. Design: docs/factory/v1/design.md.

## Success Criteria
- The test consumer rummykhan/shukka-consumer-test, whose CI file is only the caller workflow and whose config is shukka.json, deploys a throwaway project `shukkatest` (instance, elastic IP, security group, launch template, role and profile, table, bucket, DNS record in its own throwaway zone) on merge to main from a release-candidate tag
- A pull request in the test consumer shows the infrastructure diff as a comment and cannot assume the deploy roles
- A job that builds application code cannot assume the infrastructure role (observed AccessDenied)
- shukkatest's pipeline is refused on a Trendigle resource
- A destructive change stops the merge; a manual run with allow_replacement deploys it
- A deliberately unhealthy release rolls back to the previous one and the run is red
- A docs-only merge deploys nothing
- `shukka deploy` from a laptop deploys the same commit with the same guard and rollback
- shukka's own CI is green; all throwaway resources are deleted at the end
nodes.design: Components C1-C8 of the design; contracts there are binding.

nodes.title: Repository scaffold: package, TypeScript, lint, test runner, gate and shukka's own CI
nodes.description: Serves R10. Creates the structure every other task builds in.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `npm ci && npm run gate` passes on a fresh clone — run: `npm ci && npm run gate` → exit 0
- `npm run gate` runs lint, typecheck, tests, actionlint on .github/workflows and shellcheck on box/ and scripts/ shell files — run: read package.json scripts
- Tests run with node:test through tsx and print test names; a test named `<id>: …` can be selected with `--test-name-pattern` — test: one smoke test named with this task's id
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs the gate on pull requests and pushes to main, with `permissions: contents: read` and no id-token, and a secret scan (gitleaks or trufflehog, pinned by version) — run: actionlint passes; read the file
- aws-cdk-lib and constructs are peer dependencies (^2.170 / ^10) and dev dependencies; no runtime dependency outside the AWS SDK v3 clients the scripts need — run: read package.json
nodes.design: Owns package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, eslint config, .github/workflows/test.yml, test/smoke.test.ts, lib/index.ts (empty barrel), scripts/ and box/ directories with a .gitkeep. Node 22, ES modules. Follow koujou's tests/ layout only for naming ideas.

nodes.title: shukka.json schema and loader
nodes.description: Serves R1, R8, R9 (D11). The single config read by the workflows and the CLI.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `schema/shukka.schema.json` describes exactly the `shukka.json` contract in the design (project, qualifier, aws, node, checks, infra, apps with build and server, smoke, alwaysDeploy, buildEnv) — test: the design's Trendigle example validates
- `scripts/config.mjs` loads and validates a file and exits non-zero with one line per problem: project and qualifier formats, qualifier at most 10 lowercase alphanumerics, unknown keys, missing commands, health not an http URL, app names unique — test: one case per rule
- A project name that is a prefix of another known project name (or has one as its prefix) is refused when a list of known names is given — test
- Role and stack names are derived, never written in the file: `<project>-shukka-infra|app|diff` — test: the derived names for the example
- CLI form: `node scripts/config.mjs <path> --json` prints the normalised config — test
nodes.design: Owns schema/, scripts/config.mjs, test/config.test.ts and fixtures under test/fixtures/config/. Contract: `shukka.json` section of the design.

nodes.title: Infrastructure diff guard
nodes.description: Serves R4. Port of Trendigle's diff-guard.sh (trendigle/trendigle implementation/infra/diff-guard.sh) to Node, with the same rules plus: a removed stack Output is not destructive.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `scripts/guard.mjs` reads a full `cdk diff --no-color` output on stdin; exit 0 when nothing is deleted or replaced, exit 1 with the offending lines when something is, or when the closing line `Number of stacks with differences:` is missing — test: every case in Trendigle's diff-guard.test.sh
- Real cdk diff samples stop it: removed table (orphan and destroy), replaced table name, AMI, bucket rename, instance type and user-data (may be replaced), type change — test: recorded samples copied into test/fixtures/diff/
- Colour codes are stripped before matching — test
- `[-] Output` alone passes — test
- `--allow` turns a stop into exit 0 with a notice naming what was allowed — test
- Writes a markdown section `### Guard` for the step summary when `--summary <file>` is given — test
nodes.design: Owns scripts/guard.mjs, test/guard.test.ts, test/fixtures/diff/. Samples to copy: the 12 cases in Trendigle's diff-guard.test.sh, and the real outputs recorded by the security reviewer in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rehan-Documents-Workspace-software-factory/62583049-5144-4d17-806a-e9e165f32653/scratchpad/sec-b04/out/*.txt (copy them; strip nothing but the account number if present).

nodes.title: Constructs: account stack, project boundary and execution policies, project synthesizer
nodes.description: Serves R3 (D5). Port docs/factory/v1/spikes/s2/policy.py to TypeScript constructs.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `ShukkaBoundary` produces the boundary and the two execution managed policies with exactly the statements of spike S2's policy.py for the same inputs — test: compare against s2/trendigle.json (normalised)
- Each managed policy is under 6,144 characters without whitespace for the Trendigle inputs — test
- `ssm:SendCommand` in the boundary is split: the document by ARN, instances with StringEquals on the Project tag (closes the IfExists loophole from spike S2 finding 4) — test
- No statement has Resource `*` except actions with no resource type, each listed with a comment — test: scan of the synthesized documents against an allow-list
- `ShukkaAccountStack` creates the GitHub OIDC provider (client sts.amazonaws.com) and outputs its ARN and the known project names; it can import an existing provider instead — test: synthesized template
- `shukkaSynthesizer(qualifier)` returns a DefaultStackSynthesizer using that qualifier — test
- `applyBoundary(app, project)` sets the boundary on every role in an app — test: a role in a sample stack carries it
- The simulator script runs the 58 spike cases against the construct's output — run: `AWS_PROFILE=stelking node test/simulate/run.mjs` → 58 ok (needs AWS, read-only; not in the gate)
nodes.design: Owns lib/boundary.ts, lib/account-stack.ts, lib/synthesizer.ts, test/fence.test.ts, test/simulate/. Shares lib/index.ts with `access`: add exports only, expect to rebase. Contract: ShukkaBoundary and Shukka-Account sections of the design.

nodes.title: Construct: ShukkaAccess (infra, app and diff roles with workflow-scoped trust)
nodes.description: Serves R2, R4 (D3, D10). Spike S1 fixed the trust shape.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Each role's trust has aud=sts.amazonaws.com, sub StringEquals `repo:<githubRepo>:ref:refs/heads/main` (infra, app) or `repo:<githubRepo>:pull_request` (diff), and job_workflow_ref StringLike `rummykhan/shukka/.github/workflows/infra.yml@refs/tags/<versions>` (infra, diff) or `.../ec2.yml@refs/tags/<versions>` (app) — test: synthesized template, one assertion per condition per role
- No pattern starts with `*` and `githubRepo` is validated (owner/repo or the immutable `owner@id/repo@id`) — test
- Infra role may only sts:AssumeRole the project-qualifier bootstrap roles; app role exactly the permissions in the design; diff role only cloudformation:GetTemplate and DescribeStacks on the project's stacks and the bootstrap version parameter — test
- The provider is imported by ARN (from the account stack), never created by this construct — test
- `shukkaVersions` defaults to `v1*`; an `allowBranch` option exists only for release-candidate testing and is off by default — test
nodes.design: Owns lib/access.ts, test/access.test.ts. Shares lib/index.ts with `fence`: add exports only, expect to rebase. Contract: ShukkaAccess section of the design.

nodes.title: Server release script with rollback, tested in Docker
nodes.description: Serves R5 (D6).
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `box/shukka-release.sh` implements the contract in the design: arguments, exit codes 0/10/11/12/13, last line format — test: Docker harness, one case each
- Configure failure switches nothing and deletes the new release — test
- Unhealthy release rolls back to `previous`, restarts it and checks it — test
- Two releases of one app at once are serialised by flock; releases of two apps on one box do not wait for each other and one app's release leaves the other running — test
- Keeps the last 5 releases; `current/REVISION` holds the sha — test
- Never prints the contents of settings files — test: a fixture secret is absent from output
- shellcheck clean — run: gate
nodes.design: Owns box/shukka-release.sh, test/box/ (Dockerfile with a fake systemctl shim, two fake apps that serve /health, run.sh selecting cases by task id). Contract: shukka-release.sh section of the design. The script downloads with `aws s3 cp`; the harness stubs `aws` with a local file copy.

nodes.title: Scripts: upload a bundle and run a release through SSM; Next.js bundle helper
nodes.description: Serves R5, R8. Called by ec2.yml and the CLI.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `scripts/upload.mjs` uploads a directory as `s3://<bucket>/<project>/<app>/<sha>.tgz` (tar without macOS extended attributes, `.env*` refused) — test with a stubbed S3 client
- `scripts/release.mjs` sends box/shukka-release.sh with arguments through SSM Run Command to instances tagged Project=<project>, waits, prints the script output, and maps its exit code to a failure message per code — test with a stubbed SSM client
- The configure hook is read from the git checkout path given, never from the bundle — test
- `scripts/bundle.sh` turns a Next.js standalone build into a deployable directory (static, public, no .env) and prints its path — test against a fixture build tree
- shellcheck clean — run: gate
nodes.design: Owns scripts/upload.mjs, scripts/release.mjs, scripts/bundle.sh, their tests. Uses the exit-code contract of box/shukka-release.sh from the design (do not wait for `release`).

nodes.title: Scripts: what changed since the last deploy
nodes.description: Serves R7 (D7).
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `scripts/changed.mjs` prints JSON `{infra: bool, apps: {<name>: bool}, base: {infra: sha|null, apps: {...}}}` using the last deployed revisions: the `shukka:revision` tag on the project's stacks and each app's `current/REVISION` on the server — test with stubbed AWS clients and a fixture git repo
- A path change is matched with the config's globs; a docs-only change gives all false — test
- An unknown last revision (first deploy, missing tag, unreachable server) means `true` for that part — test
- `alwaysDeploy` or `--force` gives all true — test
nodes.design: Owns scripts/changed.mjs, test/changed.test.ts. Reads config through scripts/config.mjs.

nodes.title: Reusable workflows: pipeline.yml, infra.yml, ec2.yml
nodes.description: Serves R1, R4, R5, R6, R7 (C1-C3, D3, D4, D8, D10).
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `pipeline.yml` jobs and permissions match the design: plan, checks and build with contents read only and no id-token, infra via `./.github/workflows/infra.yml`, app matrix via `./.github/workflows/ec2.yml`, smoke without id-token — run: actionlint, and a test that parses the YAML and asserts no job outside infra.yml and ec2.yml has id-token
- No `${{ }}` from inputs, events or matrix is interpolated directly in `run:`; all go through `env:` — test: YAML scan
- Pull requests run plan, checks and diff (diff role, comment marked `<!-- shukka:diff -->` updated in place); merges run the full chain; workflow_dispatch passes allow_replacement and force — run: test consumer in the QA task
- infra.yml tags stacks `shukka:revision=<sha>` on deploy and writes `### Infrastructure changes` and `### Guard` to the step summary — run: test consumer
- ec2.yml checks out the repository without installing anything, downloads the artifact, uploads, releases, with concurrency `shukka-<project>-<app>` and cancel-in-progress false — test: YAML assertions
- A docs-only merge runs no deploy job — run: test consumer
nodes.design: Owns .github/workflows/pipeline.yml, infra.yml, ec2.yml, test/workflows.test.ts. Calls the scripts by path from the shukka checkout at the same ref (`actions/checkout` of rummykhan/shukka into ./.shukka at the exact commit the caller resolved: find out what GitHub exposes for this; the OIDC token's `job_workflow_sha` claim is one known source; if nothing reliable exists, fall back to a `shukka_ref` input in the caller and say so in the report. Spike S1's workflows on branch spike-s1 are a working starting point for nesting.). Pin third-party actions by full commit sha.

nodes.title: CLI: bootstrap, diff and emergency deploy
nodes.description: Serves R3, R8, R9 (C7).
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `shukka bootstrap --account` deploys ShukkaAccountStack with the caller's credentials and can import an existing OIDC provider — test: dry run prints the cdk commands; real run in the QA task
- `shukka bootstrap <project>` deploys the project's boundary and execution policies, runs `cdk bootstrap --qualifier <q> --cloudformation-execution-policies <a>,<b> --custom-permissions-boundary <boundary>`, and copies `buildEnv` values from Parameter Store to GitHub repository variables with `gh variable set` — test: dry run output
- `shukka diff` and `shukka deploy` refuse unless the working tree is clean and HEAD equals origin/main, then run the same config, guard, upload and release modules as the workflows — test: refusal cases; dry run
- `--help` documents every command — test
nodes.design: Owns bin/shukka, scripts/cli/*.mjs, test/cli.test.ts. Uses config, guard, upload, release modules; adds none of its own logic for those.

nodes.title: README: consumer guide, security model, emergency path
nodes.description: Serves R1, R8.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- README explains in order: what shukka does, the security model (who can reach which role, what the fence stops, what it does not), adopting it (account bootstrap, project bootstrap, ShukkaAccess, synthesizer, shukka.json, caller workflow), the destructive-change path, the rollback, the emergency deploy, versioning and pins, cost — run: a reader follows it in the QA task to set up the test consumer
- `docs/consumer-checklist.md` lists every step a new project takes, each with its command — run: used by the QA task
nodes.design: Owns README.md, docs/consumer-checklist.md. Written after the workflows and CLI exist; follow their real flags.

nodes.title: Acceptance suite against the test consumer and throwaway resources
nodes.description: Serves R1-R8, R10. Built by factory-tester from the requirements and design, not the implementation.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Every acceptance line of R1-R8 and every success criterion of this epic has a named step in `test/acceptance/` or a stated reason it is manual — run: read the coverage table in test/acceptance/README.md
- `bash test/acceptance/run.sh <rc-tag>` sets up `shukkatest` (account stack import, project bootstrap, shukkatest stacks in the test consumer), runs every case, and tears down every throwaway resource it created, even after a failure — run: the command, then `aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=Project,Values=shukkatest` → empty
- Trust is observed, not reasoned: AccessDenied from a pull request, from a non-main branch, from a job outside infra.yml, and for shukkatest credentials on a Trendigle resource — run: the suite's log lines `RESULT <case> DENIED`
- Rollback is observed: an unhealthy release leaves the previous REVISION live — run: suite
- The throwaway hosted zone is deleted within the run (free under 12 hours) — run: suite
nodes.design: Owns test/acceptance/ and the test consumer repository's contents (rummykhan/shukka-consumer-test). May create and delete only resources named or tagged `shukkatest*` in account 818221194501 and the throwaway zone; never touches Trendigle or Orbitary resources except the read-only refusal check. Stops if a teardown fails and reports what is left.

nodes.title: Trendigle deploys through shukka
nodes.description:
Serves R9, and R3 and R5 on the real project. Design: Rollout steps 4-6.

## Success Criteria
- Trendigle's ci.yml is only the caller workflow; shukka.json holds its settings
- A merge to Trendigle main deploys infrastructure and both apps through shukka, the CDK diff of the switch shows only role, boundary and synthesizer changes, and the smoke test passes
- Trendigle's stacks deploy through the trendigle bootstrap with the limited execution role
- The GitHub OIDC provider lives in Shukka-Account and still exists
- One deliberately unhealthy admin release rolled back on the real server (owner's leave P8)
- After two clean deploys, the old roles and the diff guard script are gone and shukka is tagged v1.0.0 and v1
nodes.design: Changes in trendigle/trendigle on branch factory/<epic-id>; production steps by the orchestrator with the owner's leave (P3, P4, P8, P9).

nodes.title: Trendigle Ci stack releases the OIDC provider (RETAIN, then remove)
nodes.description: Design risk: the provider must survive leaving the stack. Two merges or two manual Ci deploys under the old admin execution role.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Step 1 deploys the custom resource with DeletionPolicy Retain and nothing else changes — run: cdk diff shows only the policy change; `aws iam list-open-id-connect-providers` lists the provider after
- Step 2 removes it from the stack; the guard shows the removal and it is allowed by hand — run: same check after
- Step 3 `shukka bootstrap --account` imports the provider into Shukka-Account — run: describe-stacks output has the provider ARN
- Trendigle's app deploy still works after each step — run: a CI run on main or the existing deploy role assumed in a test
nodes.design: Owns implementation/infra/stacks/ci-stack.ts in Trendigle. Production steps run by the orchestrator, one at a time, provider listed between steps.

nodes.title: Bootstrap Trendigle into its own fence
nodes.description: P4. `shukka bootstrap trendigle`.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- CDKToolkit-trendigle exists with qualifier trendigle, the two execution policies and the boundary — run: describe-stacks and get-role on cdk-trendigle-cfn-exec-role
- LEGAL_ENTITY and CONTACT_EMAIL are GitHub repository variables in trendigle/trendigle (P9) — run: gh variable list
- The default bootstrap is untouched (Orbitary still uses it) — run: describe-stacks CDKToolkit unchanged
nodes.design: Ops task, no code. Run by the orchestrator.

nodes.title: Trendigle CDK: ShukkaAccess, boundary on every role, project synthesizer
nodes.description: Serves R9, R3.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Ci stack uses ShukkaAccess with the imported provider; the old github-deploy and github-infra roles stay until cleanup — run: cdk synth; cdk diff against prod shows only added roles and policies and boundary attachments
- Every stack uses shukkaSynthesizer('trendigle') and applyBoundary — run: cdk diff shows no resource replacement (guard passes)
- The infra tsc and tests pass — run: `npx tsc --noEmit` in implementation/infra
nodes.design: Owns implementation/infra/app.ts, stacks/*.ts (except changes owned by `oidc`), infra package.json (adds shukka as git dependency from the rc tag).

nodes.title: Trendigle server: configure hooks and units on release directories
nodes.description: Serves R5 on Trendigle.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- box/install.sh is split into configure-app.sh and configure-admin.sh following the hook contract (idempotent, never restarts units, units point at /opt/trendigle/<app>/current) — test: run both in shukka's Docker harness with Trendigle's settings stubbed
- The first release migrates from /opt/trendigle/app without losing settings; the old directory stays until the second successful release — test: harness case starting from today's layout
- Caddy configuration unchanged — test: rendered Caddyfile identical
nodes.design: Owns implementation/infra/box/. Uses shukka's harness from the rc tag.

nodes.title: Trendigle CI: shukka.json and the caller workflow
nodes.description: Serves R9.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- `shukka.json` validates and matches today's commands, apps, health URLs and smoke — run: `node .shukka/scripts/config.mjs shukka.json`
- ci.yml is the caller only — run: read the file; actionlint
- README and FACTORY.md describe deploying through shukka; diff-guard.sh, its test and deploy.sh's deploy path are removed or point at `shukka deploy` — run: read
nodes.design: Owns shukka.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, README section 4, FACTORY.md commands and deploy policy, implementation/infra/deploy.sh, diff-guard*.sh.

nodes.title: Switch-over merge and validation on production
nodes.description: Merge the Trendigle branch in a quiet moment with the owner's approval and watch everything.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- The merge's run: diff only expected changes, guard passed, infra deployed through the trendigle bootstrap, both apps released, smoke green — run: gh run view
- Server reports the merged sha in /opt/trendigle/app/current/REVISION and admin likewise — run: ssm send-command cat (read-only)
- One deliberately unhealthy admin release rolls back and the site stays up (P8) — run: CI run red with exit 12; curl the admin login and the site
- A second normal deploy is clean — run: gh run view
nodes.design: Ops task by the orchestrator.

nodes.title: Remove the old roles and default-bootstrap use; tag shukka v1.0.0
nodes.description: Rollout step 6.
nodes.acceptance_criteria:
- Old github-deploy and github-infra roles removed from Trendigle's Ci stack and from IAM — run: aws iam get-role → NoSuchEntity
- `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` and `AWS_INFRA_ROLE_ARN` variables removed — run: gh variable list
- shukka tagged v1.0.0 and v1; Trendigle pins v1 — run: git tag; Trendigle ci.yml
nodes.design: Trendigle Ci stack and variables; shukka tags.
